correctness.rationale: For each peripheral clique, the union of the open neighborhoods of any two distinct blade vertices is exactly that blade together with the center, so a third blade vertex cannot be legal. If the center is chosen after any peripheral vertex, all vertices are then totally dominated, forcing the center to be terminal in any maximum sequence that contains it. These bounds force exactly the two stated maximum-set profiles, and direct footprint arguments show every claimed ordering is legal. The resulting product-sum counts are exact. The included subset-DP verifier independently confirms the classification and counts on 33 heterogeneous profiles through order 13; the general theorem rests on the proof, not on the finite replay.

value.rationale: The theorem upgrades a scalar obtainable from modular decomposition to complete extremizer structure on a natural heterogeneous clique-bouquet family. It identifies two distinct maximum mechanisms, gives exact maximum-set multiplicities, and counts every ordered greedy realization. The factorial ordering counts record information discarded by the scalar recurrence and are directly relevant to multiplicity/uniqueness questions for greedy domination sequences.
